control_flow: stopAtWall: if no obstacle is ahead, stop; else call followLine.
followLine: if the line tracker sees black, curve left; else curve right.

likely_intent.description: Drive to the wall and stop before it.

decision_points.condition: first: no obstacle is ahead (FRONT); else an obstacle is ahead

branches.outcome: something is ahead: it follows the line

equivalence_classes: so far that the robot has to drive up to it
input_dimensions.dimension: how far ahead the wall is

equivalence_classes: so close that the sensor sees it at the start
input_dimensions.dimension: how far ahead the wall is

scenarios.coded_response: It stops at once while nothing is in front; with a wall in front it follows the line, turning, until the wall leaves its view, and stops
scenarios.initial_condition: On a line, in bright light, a wall stands across the line ahead of the robot: far enough to drive up to, or right in front of it
scenarios.trigger: The obstacle sensor sees the wall
scenarios.title: Stops at the wall ahead
assumptions: You didn't say how far from the wall it should stop.
It drives along the line to the wall, as your program has a line follower.
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It drives along the line and stops before the wall without bumping into it

uncertainties: Your program stops as soon as nothing is in front and follows the line only while something is in front: the reverse of what you said.
With a wall right in front it curves away until the wall leaves the sensors' view; whether it touches the wall on the way depends on the curve.
You said nothing about what it should do where there is no wall, so that situation is not tested.

postconditions.description: By the end of the run, the robot has touched Goal 1 near the wall.
During the whole run, the robot never bumps into Wall 1.
